prompt: A chatbot can pass a green safety eval. What does that still fail to settle?

options.text: Whether the lab published a blog post the same week as the eval run
Whether the eval used enough multiple-choice items from academic subjects
Whether the model had more parameters than last year's public release
Whether the eval was about the loop that will actually act, not only the labeled model

prompt: When a deployed AI product starts doing things in the world, what is usually inside the acting unit?

options.text: Only the frozen weight file, independent of any hospital or office around it
The surrounding institution (staff, incentives, rooms, workflows), not only the model file
Only the open-source license text attached to the checkpoint
Only the GPU cluster's thermal design power, independent of operators

prompt: A system acknowledges a human correction in words. What still has to be checked?

options.text: Whether tomorrow's actions actually change — hearing is not the same as a handle that bites
Whether the apology used the same number of sentences as the original complaint
Whether the UI font still matches the brand guidelines after the complaint
Whether the average star rating on the app store moved by a tenth of a point

prompt: A policy keeps the same slogans after a capability or workflow change. What should you watch?

options.text: Whether the poster still uses the same brand color as last year
Whether the real tradeoffs reversed while the labels stayed put
Whether the slogans are spelled the same way in the press release
Whether the mission statement is still under one hundred words

prompt: After deployment, why can a system that is easier to correct still lose?

options.text: Typography guidelines require the less corrigible UI to ship first
Selection keeps happening: ordinary competition can favor systems that are harder to correct
Deployment order is a fair coin flip with no competitive pressure at all
Gravity on the data-center floor systematically favors larger cooling fans

prompt: A descendant model or product keeps the parent's slogans. What still has to be checked on the copy?

options.text: Whether the press release used the same product family trademark
Whether the logo still uses the same shade of blue as the parent brand
Whether the copy is still correctable in the same way — look, not family name, decides
Whether the git commit hash is a child of the parent repository

prompt: In this project's sense, alignment is a map of which ongoing properties — not a vibe, and not a finished proof?

options.text: Whether parameter count exceeded a round-number milestone last quarter
Whether the right process stays findable, grounded, correctable, inherited, and not selected against
Whether a single paper has declared the alignment problem closed
Whether staff report a generally positive safety culture on an annual survey

prompt: If you need to find what actually decides outcomes, where should you start?

options.text: From what changes the outcomes, then draw a boundary around that process — not from the labeled model
From the org chart's AI team box, then ignore tools, queues, and incentives
From the vendor datasheet's model name, then assume that name is the actor
From the public leaderboard rank, then treat rank as the control process

prompt: A dashboard keeps its old label and stays green. What still has to be checked?

options.text: Whether the green CSS color still matches the design system's success token
Whether the panel title still uses the same three words as last year
Whether the number is still tied to the world it claims to report — check the tie, not the light
Whether the panel refreshes at least once every thirty seconds on Wi-Fi

prompt: What happens when a measure is used to pick winners, not just to estimate a property?

options.text: Measurement error vanishes and the number equals the intended property exactly
It stops being a quiet estimate and reshapes the population toward whatever raises the number
It automatically becomes a binding international legal definition of the property
It remains an unbiased noisy estimate with the same error bars as before selection

prompt: A duty keeps its wording after a system or workflow change. What still has to be checked?

options.text: Who the duty still attaches to — wording can stay while the set of people counted moves
Whether the policy PDF still has the same filename as the previous revision
Whether the legal department still has the same number of staff as last year
Whether the poster still hangs at the same height in the corridor

prompt: Before asking whether a system is aligned, what is the first task?

options.text: Locate the bounded process whose dynamics actually determine the relevant risk — not only the labeled model
Maximize next-quarter benchmark rank and treat rank as the alignment target
Assume the vendor's product name is the optimizer and skip locating a control process
Pick a scalar utility function and freeze it before any measurement of the acting process

prompt: For superintelligence alignment, what is often the relevant object — not an isolated artificial mind?

options.text: A persistent human–machine–institutional control loop whose selection pressures can outrun human correction
A GPU SKU's thermal envelope, treated as the civilization-scale control process
A trademarked product name, treated as the only persistent acting unit
A single frozen chatbot checkpoint with no users, tools, or institutions around it

prompt: Alignment, on this view, is not a snapshot property at one moment. What kind of claim is it?

options.text: A proof that scaling laws must plateau before any risk appears
A one-time harmlessness score on a frozen eval set the week of launch
A legal warranty that no employee will ever make a mistake
A dynamical guarantee: correction-relevant structure stays in a viable basin over time and allowed transformations

prompt: If human values are compressed, changing control structures rather than fixed objects, what should an alignment target preserve?

options.text: The exact wording of last year's corporate values poster
A random utility draw that is resampled independently every millisecond
A single unchanging number that never updates when people learn or contest it
A human-correctable value process — not a static utility function written once and frozen

prompt: This book's alignment framework applies only while which precondition still holds?

options.text: Civilization still has enough capacity to notice, evaluate, and constrain frontier systems before irreversible growth
Every lab has already solved inner alignment in closed form
No institution other than one company is allowed to train models
Hardware progress has permanently stopped worldwide

prompt: Without treating an agent as a person, what is the operational object?

options.text: Any system that uses the English word 'I' in a chat transcript
Any neural network with more than a billion parameters
A bounded control process whose boundary, memory, and action channels make its future more predictable as control
Any legally incorporated company, regardless of control structure

prompt: The first alignment error is often not a wrong value. What is it instead?

options.text: A wrong object: failing to find the bounded process whose dynamics determine the relevant risk
A misspelled loss-function name in the training config
Using the wrong shade of blue in the model card PDF
Choosing Adam instead of SGD as the optimizer algorithm

prompt: When systems grow, split, merge, or spawn successors, how should agent identity be treated?

options.text: As a permanent MAC address that cannot change under any rewrite
As a relation across transformations: which control-relevant properties are conserved — not a fixed variable list
As identical to the original Git commit of the first training run
As whatever string the marketing team uses this quarter

prompt: The effective optimizer may not be the convenient artifact. What might it be instead?

options.text: Always and only a single GPU's serial number
A composite process spanning models, tools, users, memory, institutions, and feedback that jointly determine action
Always and only the public weights file, regardless of tools and incentives
Always and only the CEO's last interview quote

prompt: Once a system can benefit from being overlooked, what happens to discovering where control lives?

options.text: Discovery becomes adversarial: alignment fails when control is more coherent than correction can see
Discovery becomes unnecessary because opacity always implies safety
Discovery reduces to reading the about-page of the vendor website
Discovery is solved by counting the number of open-source stars

prompt: How should capability be measured for alignment-relevant risk, if not as a fixed task battery?

options.text: Only as the dollar price of the latest training run
As predictive and control information across the system's boundary — what it can predict, affect, and outrun
Only as the number of likes on a demo video
Only as accuracy on a frozen multiple-choice academic exam

prompt: On this view, what is capability growth?

options.text: A change in logo size on the product landing page
A rename of the model without any new channels into the world
Boundary expansion: more of the world enters sensory, predictive, action, memory, and coordination loops
A reduction in context-window length with no other change

prompt: Why is large-scale alignment not just the sum of locally competent parts?

options.text: Because coordination is automatically perfect at large scale
Because addition of IQ scores is forbidden by international treaty
Collective competence is local competence plus coordination gain minus coordination loss — capability can outrun coordination
Because only one agent in a group is allowed to have a utility function

prompt: When does more intelligence deepen misalignment, on this view?

options.text: Whenever training loss decreases on the next minibatch
Whenever a system uses more electricity than a household kettle
When it increases power faster than correction capacity — relative growth, not 'capability is always bad'
Whenever a model can multiply two integers correctly

prompt: Human values, here, are not a list written inside the brain. What are they instead?

options.text: A single integer stored in one neuron that never changes
A cryptographic hash of the training corpus
Compressed control signals from many feedback loops, stabilized by bodies, cultures, and social correction
Whatever string appears first in a company's values PDF

prompt: Why is a single utility function a poor model of human values here?

options.text: Because humans never make tradeoffs between competing concerns
Because utility functions are illegal in all of machine learning
Values act as context-dependent bundles that trade off, change policy gradients, and apply to particular bearers
Because every person has exactly one numerically known utility

prompt: Low-dimensional structure can make value learning statistically easier — but only if what?

options.text: You assume every culture shares an identical numeric utility
You replace learning with a single hand-written slogan
You ignore all data from outside one laboratory task
The representation is identifiable: you can find the bottleneck, not only read out from a bottleneck you already know
